fun_highlights: The callback arc genuinely rewards patience. cb_lookaway delivering 'Stopped, this time, for the person most would pass — and paid, to someone who would never know it, a debt 27 years overdue' (Hale Okonkwo, Dynasty 4) is the exact warm payoff a cozy player wants: a small wrong from childhood closing quietly in middle age. These reach-back moments are the game's best writing.

Trait-shaped prose in the observation layer is doing real atmospheric work. A 'warm' character getting 'Carried a warmth into every room, and left it there' as their epitaph; a frail one spending strength 'like a careful coin' (Cassian Thorne); a dreaming one chasing 'the thing only she could see' — the writing varies enough by who the person IS that reading three consecutive 'bright' characters still feels like three different people.

The dynasty layer delivers genuine cozy pull. Watching House Okonkwo's motto crystallise to 'We earn the bread we eat.' at Noor's death, then seeing Beatrix born already knowing that phrase, genuinely felt like accumulation. The heirloom prose ('a book too hard for a child's hands', 'a soft spot for strays') is concise and evocative. This is the layer that makes 'one more life' feel like 'one more chapter of the same story.'

Era variety is doing useful texture work. The plague framing ('A sickness is moving through the country — slow, and close') in Dynasty 4/6/7 shapes the calling card prompt differently ('There is a war on, and it is hungry for the young') and produces genuinely different felt contexts even when the underlying card is structurally identical. Born-into-plenty vs. born-into-hardship reads as a real difference.

Early childhood moments with the stray and the book are sweet entry points. Dynasty 7's Cleo 'hid a stray and fed it in secret, and learned young the weight of a thing that depends on you' — then the soft-spot heirloom propagating to her daughter Felix Aldecott — is the cozy inheritance fantasy working cleanly.

Short lives (Joaquin at 16, Linnea at 18, Theda at 10) genuinely land as melancholy rather than punishment. 'Gone too soon, with so much unspent' and 'Left before the story had found its middle' are correctly weighted — a cozy player feels the ache without feeling cheated.
staleness: The calling card (y_calling) is the single biggest structural repetition signal. Across the 15 dynasties every called life hits the same four bullet choices in the same mid-teens age window, and the log lines that follow are almost verbatim: 'Chose study, and hunger, and the long bet on his own head' appears functionally in Dynasty 1 (Saoirse soldier), Dynasty 2 (Henrik scholar), Dynasty 3 (Cassian maker), Dynasty 4 (Calla wanderer), Dynasty 6 (Tomas scholar), etc. By session midpoint the player knows what beat is coming the moment a life hits 14-22.

The 'Meet them halfway / Pretend not to notice' love beat fires in nearly every multi-generation dynasty and the log line pools are thin enough that exact phrases repeat: 'Started, without quite deciding to, building the days around another person' appears in Tomas Thorne (D6), Ingrid Thorne (D6-4th), Annika Brandt (D15), Anders Aldecott (D14-2nd). Even the marriage lines cycle visibly: 'The day was small and the meaning was not' recurs verbatim in Dynasty 10 (Tobias) and Dynasty 14 (Greta), and the 'nobody made a speech; the years that followed were the speech' variant shows up in Dynasty 10 Felix.

The body-decline observation cluster (vit_tire, vit_neg) is the most tonally flat zone in a long session. Reading 15 dynasties back-to-back, the engine hits the 40+ vit-low trigger in almost every second life, and phrases like 'The stairs have started to ask a question of them' and 'Mornings take longer to arrive in the body than they once did' appear across Dynasty 2 Henrik (age 85), Dynasty 4 Hale (age 53), Dynasty 6 Cassian Thorne (age 57), Dynasty 13 Idris (age 55), Dynasty 13 Anders (age 74 and 81). The per-life cap of 4 (_obsN) stops the flood but 'the body keeps its own ledger now' landing in four separate dynasties inside one session still reads as a template.

The 'reputation reckoning / building from nothing' adult pair (s_from_nothing + a_make_name) fire in nearly every low-seat adult life and produce nearly identical log lines. 'Began from nothing, and laid the first course of something, alone' appears in Saoirse D1, Cassian Achterberg D3, Ottilie D5, Mira Halloran D12. The structural beat (I have nothing → choose to build or climb with others) is the same scene every time.

Epitaphs collapse to roughly four clusters in a long session. Scanning the 15 dynasties: 'Built something that outlasted the building of it' (Saoirse D1, Tobias D10), 'Gave away everything she knew, and so kept it' (Henrik D2, Selma D9), 'Left people gentler than he found them' (Elias Okonkwo D4, Idris D13), 'Was elsewhere as often as here, and the elsewhere was wide' (Saoirse D15-3rd, Anders D14-2nd). The session-wide RECENT_CLUSTERS blocking works somewhat, but with 15 dynasties the pool exhaustion still shows.

The 'war reaches into the house' grief beat (choosing 'Bury it in work' or 'Let the grief in') fires in Dynasty 4 (Elias and Noor both), Dynasty 5 (Cassian Thorne), Dynasty 7 (Caleb Castellane), Dynasty 14 (Anders Aldecott-2nd) — and each time the log line is essentially 'Lost someone to the war and put the loss away in work, where it kept, badly, for years.' The phrasing is near-identical across five uses, and in Dynasty 4 it lands in consecutive generations.

improvements.what: Add 3-4 additional log-line variants per choice in the love and marriage beats (y_love1, a_marry), with stronger personalisation by vocation. A maker falling in love should echo the bench and the hands; a wanderer's marriage should taste of choosing a door over a horizon more vividly than 'The day was small and the meaning was not.'
improvements.why: These are the highest-frequency beats in the transcript. With 7 'Meet them halfway' variants and 10 marriage lines, exact repetition still surfaced across 15 dynasties. Vocation-keyed variants already exist for a_marry's prompt text but not for the log lines themselves — the payoff prose is the part the player reads twice.

improvements.what: Cap the vit_tire body-decline observation to 2 fires per 10-dynasty window using the existing RECENT_CLUSTERS / session-level mechanism, and widen the pool by 4-5 lines that are more situationally specific (a soldier's tired body reading differently from a scholar's, a wanderer's different from a maker's). The current per-life cap of 4 stops intra-life flood; it doesn't stop the cross-dynasty sameness.
improvements.why: Body decline is the single most visible repeated texture in a long session. The vit_tire pool has 18 entries but they share the same register ('stairs', 'body keeps its own ledger', 'mornings arrive late') — five distinct metaphors, all saying the same thing. A soldier's 'the wounds have opinions now' and a scholar's 'the mind outruns the hands' are different colours of old age.

improvements.what: Add a 5th and 6th calling option — 'the healer's road' or 'the farmer's ground' — with their own thin arc, so the 4-option fork at 14-22 isn't always identical. Even one new option that appears only in certain eras (e.g. healer only available in plague eras) would break the recognition pattern without requiring a full new vocation arc.
improvements.why: The calling fork is the single most visually repeated prompt in the transcript. Even with the era-sensitive framing text, the four bullet choices are word-for-word identical across every called life in every dynasty. A cozy player is hitting 'which life shall I pick this time' within the first two dynasties, and by dynasty 8 the fork feels like a template rather than a question.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 'war grief' log-line variants keyed to relationship type (spouse lost vs. friend lost vs. sibling lost) and restrict the 'lost someone to the war and put the loss away in work' line to a once-per-session pool rather than a per-dynasty once. The current onceDyn cooldown isn't preventing it from appearing in 5 of 15 dynasties.
improvements.why: The war-loss beat firing with near-identical phrasing in consecutive generations within Dynasty 4 (Elias then Noor) and across Dynasties 4/6/7/14 is the most jarring specific repetition in the transcript. A parent losing a spouse reads differently from a soldier losing a comrade; the grief deserves differentiated language.

improvements.what: Add one or two 'midlife synthesis' cards that can only fire after specific combinations of earlier choices — something that only a person who both 'chose study young' AND 'refused to teach their knowledge' can face, for example. These needle-in-haystack cards create the sense that a life is truly unrepeatable, not just randomly assembled.
improvements.why: The callback system (cb_lookaway, cb_books_late, cb_principle) is the game's best staleness defence and is responsible for most of the highlights above. But it currently reaches back only to single flags. A card that asks 'you built the name AND strayed AND never confessed — what does the house feel like from inside that contradiction?' would be uniquely memorable. The engine already tracks all the necessary flags.

verdict: A Life has real warmth and a dynasty layer that earns genuine 'one more generation' pull; the callback arcs (lookaway, books, principle) are genuinely affecting and the heirloom/motto accumulation delivers the cozy inheritance fantasy cleanly. The writing quality is high — individual lines land well, and trait-shaped prose gives characters texture. But a 15-dynasty session exposes the template underneath: the calling fork, the love beat, the body-decline observations, and the war-grief line all recur with enough textual similarity that by mid-session a cozy player is completing the prose before it arrives. The game is most comfortable in its first 4-5 dynasties; staleness sets in steadily after that, which is exactly the threshold where this genre needs to stay fresh.
